author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Alpine Swift (Tachymarptis melba), adult in flight seen from below: upperparts uniform dull grey-brown; a white throat patch; a broad brown band across the breast; belly white; vent, undertail coverts and undertail dark brown; underwing dark brown; dark eye; tiny black bill.
art.pose: in flight seen from below, wings outstretched in a scythe shape, head, body and tail in one line
art.scene: Sea cliffs on a Korean offshore island in spring, swifts sweeping across a clear blue sky; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Very large swift, much larger than Pacific Swift (Apus pacificus) and far bulkier than a Barn Swallow; cigar-shaped body, long, narrow, scythe-shaped wings and a short tail with a shallow fork. Tiny bill with a wide gape; tiny feathered feet, almost never seen. Flight powerful and fast, with slower, deeper wingbeats than smaller swifts and long glides; it never perches on wires or branches and only clings to cliffs.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump; that marks Pacific Swift and House Swift.
Do not join the white throat to the white belly; a brown breast band separates them.
Do not paint a deeply forked tail or long swallow-like tail streamers.
Do not show it perched on a wire or twig.
